description: Hey there! I am Abdelaziz, a computer engineer who is doing his masters in cybersecurity. I am interested in building applications and tools that makes the life much easier. I am joining this hackathon with the goals of learning new things, meeting smart people, and having fun. I am interested in working on Space mission design game challenge. Join my team if you are passionate and plan to spend the next 2 days learning and exploring how to build the winning game for that hackathon!
summary:
Mission Forge is a 3D educational game developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026’s Space Mission Design Game challenge. Players become mission engineers tasked with designing, assembling and operating a satellite for Flood Watch, an Earth-observation mission.

Players explore themed rooms, learn space-engineering concepts and choose a sensor, power system, radio, orbit, launcher and propellant. Every decision creates trade-offs across budget, mass, power, battery capacity, data storage and communications. A stronger instrument, for example, collects more detailed observations but demands more energy and storage.

The game supports single-player exploration and 2–4-player cooperative play, with teammates sharing engineering responsibilities. After assembling the satellite and passing readiness checks, players launch their design and follow its operations using real GMAT-generated orbital trajectories and a simplified resource simulation.

Success requires delivering useful observations to Earth without energy shortages or data loss. Through clear objectives, interactive learning and visible consequences, Mission Forge demonstrates that a successful space mission depends on balancing an entire connected system.
details:
Mission Forge is a 3D educational game created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026’s Space Mission Design Game challenge. Players become engineers designing a satellite mission called Flood Watch, with the objective of delivering useful Earth-observation data while avoiding energy shortages and data loss.

Players explore themed engineering rooms and select a sensor, power system, radio, orbit, launcher and propellant. Each choice affects interconnected constraints, including budget, mass, electrical demand, battery capacity, storage and communications. Players assemble their contributions, validate the complete design and launch their mission.

The game supports single-player exploration and cooperative play for 2–4 players, with engineering responsibilities distributed among teammates. An interactive library, progress guidance and visible validation feedback help players understand their decisions.

We developed the game using Python, Ursina and Panda3D, with NASA’s GMAT providing orbital trajectories. The game calculates simplified resource behaviour from those trajectories and uses NASA Earth imagery for its planet visuals.

Its creative approach turns spacecraft design into a walkable, collaborative learning experience. Our intended impact is to make systems engineering accessible: players discover that improving one subsystem can create problems elsewhere, and success requires balancing the whole mission.
